_README: INDEPENDENT ORACLE for canonical rental model band assertions (Group MODEL, CI Wave 1). These £-pcm bands are HAND-VALIDATED from real London lettings-market knowledge (Q2 2026) for mainstream 1-2 bed flats with real sqft — the segment the model is documented to predict well (see MEMORY model-eval-strong-weak). They are NOT regenerated from the model: they are deliberately WIDE, generous market ranges so they form a genuine external sanity oracle (a healthy model lands comfortably inside; a geography-collapsed or size-degenerate model falls outside). Do NOT auto-update these from predict_one output — that would defeat the oracle. Each anchor's `inputs` feed canonical_predict.predict_one verbatim. `pcm_low`/`pcm_high` bound a plausible monthly rent; `note` records the rationale.

anchors.label: SW3_2bed_900_chelsea
anchors.note: Prime Chelsea 2-bed flat, ~900 sqft. Real market mid is ~£5-6k pcm; band is intentionally wide on both sides for an external oracle.

anchors.label: SW7_1bed_550_southken
anchors.note: Prime South Kensington 1-bed, ~550 sqft. Mid ~£2.8-3.5k pcm.

anchors.label: E14_2bed_900_canarywharf
anchors.note: Canary Wharf 2-bed, ~900 sqft. Materially cheaper than prime SW3; mid ~£3-3.8k pcm. The SW3-vs-E14 gap is the geography-collapse guard.

anchors.label: NW8_2bed_1000_stjohnswood
anchors.note: St John's Wood 2-bed/2-bath, ~1000 sqft. Mid ~£4-4.5k pcm.

location_sensitivity._note: SW3 (prime) vs E14 (Docklands) for an IDENTICAL 2-bed 900-sqft flat must differ MEANINGFULLY in £, both ways: prime > docklands, and by at least min_gap_pcm. Guards the shipped SW3-fillna geography-collapse fix (MEMORY tail-signal-audit / geography-collapse). On a collapsed model both would predict ~the SW3 value and the gap would vanish.

freq_map_health._note: Geography-collapse guard on the frequency map itself (independent of any single prediction). The shipped fix restored 67 districts with no single REAL district dominating; the degenerate pre-fix state had ~91.5% mass in SW3 (MEMORY tail-signal-audit). UNKNOWN is a non-district aggregation bucket and is excluded from the single-district dominance check.
